summary: FireHarmonize is an interactive web app for exploring active-fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS. Our processing workflow quality-filters observations and applies biome-aware calibration to produce monthly fire counts and fire radiative power (FRP) on a more comparable basis across sensors. The app presents fire locations and monthly activity in an interactive map and calendar heatmap. Its anomaly engine calculates a Standardized Fire Anomaly Index (SFAI) by comparing a region’s biome-specific monthly count with earlier observations, and uses a Chow test to look for evidence of a structural change around 2012. This helps users investigate unusually active months while seeing the sensor context behind the measurements. The current prototype provides regional and biome-level diagnostics; NOAA ONI integration and valid H3-cell anomaly output are not yet included.
details:
FireHarmonize combines satellite fire observations with a web-based exploration tool. The data workflow filters and calibrates MODIS and VIIRS observations, accounting for differences between sensors and biome types, then aggregates the results into monthly records. The web application is built with Nuxt, Vue, and TypeScript; DuckDB queries Parquet data, and NASA GIBS imagery provides a satellite map layer.

Users can explore fire locations and monthly patterns on the map and calendar heatmap. The anomaly engine compares each region’s biome-specific monthly fire count with its earlier history to calculate an SFAI score and alert category. A Chow test checks for statistical evidence of a change around the 2012 sensor transition. These are exploratory diagnostics: they do not prove that a sensor discontinuity has been eliminated or that climate conditions caused a fire increase.
